exposure: mode of labor onset (induced vs. spontaneous)
presence or absence of risk conditions
cohort: Women in Norway with a second delivery after a first pregnancy cesarean section, excluding preterm, multiple, and non-cephalic deliveries (n = 57,109)
finding: The study found that in pregnancies complicated by medical risk conditions, the lowest trial of labor rates were seen in women with diabetes type 1, diabetes type 2, maternal heart conditions, and pregnancy-related psychiatric conditions, while the highest failure rates were observed in diabetes type 1, diabetes type 2, maternal obesity, gestational diabetes, and offspring macrosomia.
mod_finding: Induced labor was associated with failed trial of labor, whereas after spontaneous labor, failure rates were less than 40% in all conditions studied.
